lines.speaker: RAVAN
lines.text: Every year, you burn me. Ten heads. Fireworks inside. Millions of you, cheering.

lines.speaker: RAVAN
lines.text: But tell me... what if the arrow had missed?

lines.speaker: ASKER
lines.text: Wait. Raavuhnuh... won?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In one universe, yes. And this is his Lanka. In the year 2026.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Chapter one. The city of gold.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The Ramayan describes it as Swarna Lanka. A city of gold, built by Vishwakarma, the architect of the gods, on an island guarded by the ocean itself.

lines.speaker: ASKER
lines.text: But wasn't Raavuhnuh just... the villain?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Not just. In the stories, Raa-vuh-nuh was a scholar. A master of the veena. A devotee of Shiva so intense, legend says he tried to lift Mount Kailash. The Shiva Tandav Stotram, still chanted today, is credited to him.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So imagine that mind... winning.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Chapter two. The empire.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: By the year one thousand, Lanka controls every sea route between Africa and China. Spice, silk, gold. All of it pays a toll to one island.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And then, the Pushpak Vimaan. In the epic, a flying chariot that moves by thought. In this world, Lankan engineers spend two thousand years rebuilding it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: By 2026, Lanka has the busiest skyport on Earth. Silent golden aircraft rise from the palace like fireflies.

lines.speaker: ASKER
lines.text: Okay, that part sounds amazing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And here's a real fact. In our world, Sri Lanka's first satellite, launched in 2019, was named after Raa-vuh-nuh himself.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Ten great towers stand around the palace. One for each of Raa-vuh-nuh's heads. Medicine. Music. Astronomy. War. Ten minds, ruling as one.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Chapter three. The shadow.

lines.speaker: ASKER
lines.text: So... where's the catch?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: There is no Dussehra here. No festival where good defeats pride. Children grow up with a different story. The strong take what they want.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The ten towers watch everything. Disagree with the king, and you don't disappear. You're simply forgotten.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And somewhere in the archives, there is a story nobody is allowed to tell. Of a woman taken from a forest, who never got to go home.

lines.speaker: ASKER
lines.text: So was he good, or bad?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That's the real question. Raa-vuh-nuh was brilliant. Powerful. Devoted. And it still wasn't enough. Even his own brother, Vibbeeshunnuh, warned him, and walked away.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Maybe that's why the story needs him to lose. Not because he was weak. But because he was so strong, that only one flaw could bring him down.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Pride.

lines.speaker: RAVAN
lines.text: So you burn me every year...

lines.speaker: RAVAN
lines.text: ...so that you never become me.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So tell me. If Raa-vuh-nuh had won, would you live in his golden Lanka? Comment yes, or no.
